findings.summary: Re-implemented `asciiTrim` uses a backtracking anchored-whitespace regex (`[\s]+$`) on attacker-controlled note text — quadratic ReDoS that can freeze the renderer thread
findings.evidence: The new lheading rule replaces upstream's native `.trim()` with `str.replace(/^[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+|[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+$/g, '')` (lines 19-23), applied at line 128 to `state.getLines(startLine, nextLine, state.blkIndent, false)` — i.e. raw, unbounded, user-authored markdown. The `[ws]+$` alternative is the classic quadratic-trim pattern: for a whitespace run that is NOT at end-of-string, the engine matches the run greedily, fails `$`, backtracks the whole run, then retries from every subsequent index → O(n^2). Attack: a collaborator types/pastes into a shared Yorkie note `a` + ~100k spaces + `b` on one line followed by `===` (or `---`), which routes into this exact code path (setext heading found ⇒ asciiTrim on the whole paragraph). Rendering the note in any viewer's browser burns ~10^9-10^10 regex steps on the main thread, hanging the tab (preview is rendered synchronously on every doc update). Upstream markdown-it deliberately avoids this by using the native trim; the re-creation is what introduces the vector. I did not execute the payload (packages/notes is not present in this checkout), hence medium confidence on the exact wall-clock cost.

findings.summary: Vendored fork of markdown-it's `lheading` plus reliance on the private `__rules__` registry silently opts the notes preview out of upstream parser security fixes
findings.evidence: `getRuleFn` (lines 204-212) reads `md.block.ruler.__rules__`, an undocumented private field, to recover the stock `list` fn, and `lheadingRule` (lines 78-153) is a hand-copied duplicate of markdown-it 14.x `rules_block/lheading.mjs`. markdown-it has shipped hardening/DoS fixes inside individual block rules before; any future patch to `lheading` is dead code here because `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', lheadingRule)` (line 174) unconditionally overwrites it, and a minor-version refactor of `__rules__` makes `getRuleFn` throw at module init (breaking preview rendering) or, if the shape merely changes, silently changes which fn is delegated to. This is a supply-chain/patch-application weakness rather than a live exploit: pinned-fork drift in a parser that sits directly on untrusted input.

findings.summary: Wrapped `list` rule returns `true` in silent mode without running the stock rule's indent/code-block/listIndent guards, widening paragraph-interruption and block-nesting amplification on untrusted input
findings.evidence: `wrappedList` (lines 180-192) short-circuits to `return true` whenever `silent && parentType === 'paragraph' && isEmptyBulletLine(...)`. `isEmptyBulletLine` (lines 31-49) only checks `sCount[line] >= blkIndent` and the marker shape; it skips the stock list rule's `sCount - blkIndent >= 4` (indented-code) and `listIndent >= 0 && sCount - listIndent >= 4` guards. Attacker-supplied input of the form `a` followed by successively-indented lone bullets now terminates paragraphs and opens a new nested list at each line where upstream would refuse, so a small document can drive block-nesting/re-tokenization much deeper than before; markdown-it's `maxNesting` (default 100) is the only remaining cap and preview.ts's options in the diff do not show it being set explicitly. I traced the missing guards by comparison with markdown-it 14 `rules_block/list.mjs` but could not measure an actual parse-time blowup or confirm a case where the non-silent pass also declines (which would surface as markdown-it's 'none of the rules matched' throw, i.e. a render-breaking exception), hence low confidence.

findings.summary: No adversarial/pathological-input test accompanies the new parser rules — only happy-path rendering cases
findings.evidence: The added tests all assert intended rendering shapes; none exercise the security-relevant edges the change creates: long whitespace runs through the new `asciiTrim` (ReDoS path), deeply/irregularly indented empty bullets through the relaxed silent-mode `list` guard (nesting amplification, potential 'none of the rules matched' throw), or that the existing XSS-escaping expectations still hold for content routed through the replaced `lheading` (e.g. `<script>alert(1)</script>\n===`). Because the package tree is not present in this checkout I could not rule out such tests living in another file, so this is medium confidence.

findings.summary: Hand-rolled `asciiTrim` regex has quadratic backtracking on attacker-controlled note text (client-side ReDoS), replacing markdown-it's native trim
findings.evidence: The vendored lheading copy trims heading content with `ASCII_TRIM_RE = /^[\x09-\x0d\x20]+|[\x09-\x0d\x20]+$/g` (line 21-22) applied via `str.replace` (line 24) to `state.getLines(startLine, nextLine, ...)` — i.e. to raw document text. The second alternative `[ws]+$` is unanchored at the start, so on a setext-heading paragraph containing a long internal whitespace run followed by a non-whitespace char (e.g. `"x" + " ".repeat(200000) + "y\n==="`), the engine retries the greedy class at every whitespace offset and backtracks to the end each time → O(n^2) work with no match. Because notes content is rendered in the browser preview and notes are collaborative (Yorkie-backed), a co-editor can paste such a line and freeze other viewers' tab (availability DoS on untrusted input). Upstream markdown-it uses a native trim here, so this is a regression introduced by re-implementing the rule. Confidence is low because I could not run the timing test — the repository working tree was not reachable from my sandbox (only the tooling/scripts directory was visible), so I reasoned from the diff text alone.

findings.summary: Plugin reads markdown-it's private `__rules__` registry and throws at wiring time if absent, turning a dependency bump into a hard render/bundle failure
findings.evidence: `getRuleFn` casts `md.block.ruler` to expose `__rules__` and does `throw new Error('markdown-it block rule not found: list')` when the private field/entry is missing. `listEmptyBulletPlugin` is applied at module scope in `preview.ts` (`md.use(listEmptyBulletPlugin)`), so any markdown-it internal rename makes the notes preview module throw on import rather than degrade — an availability failure of the whole preview surface, not just the #517 behaviour. Not attacker-triggerable, so nit; flagged only because it lives on the input-parsing path.

findings.summary: No verified bound/guard review of the new paragraph-terminator shortcut against markdown-it's tokenizer invariants; I could not open the working tree to enumerate the other rules that consume `list` in silent mode
findings.evidence: `wrappedList` returns `true` in silent mode (paragraph-terminator mode) for any empty bullet line when `state.parentType === 'paragraph'`, without delegating to the stock rule. `list` is registered in the `alt` chains `['paragraph','reference','blockquote']`, so `blockquote` (lazy-continuation checks) and `reference` also invoke it silently; the `parentType === 'paragraph'` guard looks like it confines the deviation, and a paragraph nested inside a blockquote/list still reaches it. If any caller relies on silent `list` truth implying the non-silent rule will consume the line, markdown-it can end up re-dispatching the line (`paragraph` fallback) or, in the worst case, hitting its internal "block rule didn't increment state.line" / "none of the block rules matched" throw during render of untrusted note text (parser-level DoS). I could not confirm or refute this: the repository files (packages/notes/src/view/*, node_modules/markdown-it/lib/rules_block/*) were not accessible from my sandbox, so no call-site enumeration or exception-handling check of `NotePreview.render` was possible. Reported at low confidence so a verifier with tree access can close it out.

findings.summary: Fix is scoped far wider than the issue: single-dash setext headings (`Heading\n-`) are silently killed everywhere in the notes preview
findings.evidence: `const isLoneDash = marker === DASH && runLength === 1;` in the forked `lheadingRule` rejects a lone `-` underline unconditionally — at any nesting level, including a plain top-level paragraph with no list anywhere in sight. The originating issue is narrowly about "a list item followed by an empty nested list item"; its expected behavior only concerns the parent `<li>`. After this change, existing note content such as `Title\n-` (a perfectly ordinary CommonMark H2, the single-dash form of `Title\n---`) stops being a heading and instead renders as a paragraph followed by an empty bullet list. Nothing in the issue asks for that. A guard restricted to the in-list case (e.g. only when `state.blkIndent > 0` / the paragraph is inside a list item) would satisfy the issue with no collateral. The docs added in this PR acknowledge only that "Multi-dash `---` and `=` setext underlines are untouched" (docs/design/notes/notes.md), i.e. they concede single-dash setext is broken, but the issue never requested that trade. Note also the PR's own plan (docs/tasks/active/20260724-notes-empty-bullet-setext-todo.md, "Steps") lists a `top-level lone dash` test case that does not appear among the added tests, so the widest behavior change of the PR is the one left unpinned.

findings.summary: ~85 lines of markdown-it's upstream `lheading` rule (plus its `asciiTrim` helper) are forked into the repo instead of being wrapped/delegated as the `list` rule is in the same file
findings.evidence: `const lheadingRule: BlockRule = ...` is, by its own comment, a copy of "markdown-it 14.x `rules_block/lheading.mjs`" "with a single added guard". `ASCII_TRIM_RE`/`asciiTrim` (lines 18-23) likewise re-create markdown-it's private helper. This duplicates dependency-owned logic in a repo whose stated norm is reuse: any markdown-it upgrade that touches lheading (lazy-continuation handling, terminator scanning, token map fields) silently diverges here with nothing to detect the drift. The same file demonstrates the non-forking alternative 110 lines later — `wrappedList` captures the original `list` rule and delegates for every case but the one it cares about — so the two rules in one plugin use two different, inconsistent approaches. A pre-check-then-delegate wrapper for `lheading` (decline only when the underline candidate is a lone dash, otherwise call the stock rule) would avoid carrying the fork.

findings.summary: The paragraph-interrupt relaxation covers `*` and `+` and top-level paragraphs, which is broader than the reported case
findings.evidence: `wrappedList` returns true for any `isEmptyBulletLine`, and `isEmptyBulletLine` accepts `-`, `*` and `+` (lines 38-41) with no requirement that the paragraph be inside a list item. So `foo\n*` or `foo\n+` — previously plain paragraph text per CommonMark — now terminate the paragraph and emit an empty `<ul>`. The issue only describes an indented empty bullet under a parent list item; the `*`/`+` and top-level relaxations are unrequested behavior changes and are not covered by the acceptance criteria the PR's own todo doc lists.

findings.summary: `getRuleFn` reaches into markdown-it's private `__rules__` registry to recover a rule function

findings.summary: Couples to two markdown-it private internals (`Ruler.__rules__`, hardcoded `alt` chain) — fragile abstraction layer for a rendering tweak

Inputs like `'- 1\n      -'` or `'1\n    -'` therefore hit an untested corner where the paragraph may be terminated but no list produced. No added test renders an input with more than two leading spaces.

findings.summary: Weak assertions in two of the new tests: parent content checked only with `startsWith('1')`, and the trailing-space test never asserts the nested item is actually empty
findings.evidence: `expect(outer?.textContent?.trim().startsWith('1')).toBe(true);` passes for any parent text beginning with '1' (e.g. '1-' from a lazy-continuation regression that also produced no `<h2>`), and in the `'- 1\n  - '` test the only structural assertion is `expect(preview.el.querySelector('ul > li > ul > li')).toBeTruthy();` with no check that the nested `<li>` is empty (a stray `-` leaking into it would pass). findings.summary: The `lheading` replacement is unconditional, so it also kills single-dash setext H2 at top level in every existing note — far beyond the nested-bullet case the diff claims to scope
findings.evidence:
`const isLoneDash = marker === DASH && runLength === 1;` (list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:105) and the guard at :107 have no notion of list context, nesting depth, or `state.blkIndent`/`parentType`. The rule is installed on the shared preview singleton at list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:175 (`md.block.ruler.at('lheading', lheadingRule)`), which `preview.ts` applies to the module-level `md` used for ALL note rendering. Consequence for content the diff never looks at: a plain document Heading - previously rendered `

Heading

` and now renders `

Heading

` plus an empty `
` (lheading declines, then the relaxed `list` wrapper at :184-190 terminates the paragraph and builds an empty list). Single-dash `-` is a perfectly ordinary setext H2 form, so every already-stored note using it re-renders differently after this ships. The design note added in this same change (docs/design/notes/notes.md, `Multi-dash \`---\` and \`=\` setext underlines are untouched, so ordinary setext headings still render`) describes a narrower blast radius than the code actually has, and the tests added only cover `Heading\n---`, not `Heading\n-`. Fix belongs on the new code: gate `isLoneDash` on being inside a list/indented context (e.g. `state.blkIndent > 0` or a nested-item check) rather than applying it to every paragraph in the corpus.

findings.summary: The relaxed `list` paragraph-interrupt also fires for lone `*` and `+` at top level, changing paragraph rendering for markdown `lheading` never touched
findings.evidence:
`isEmptyBulletLine` accepts all three bullet markers (`list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:39`: `if (marker !== DASH && marker !== 0x2a /* * */ && marker !== 0x2b /* + */)`), and the wrapper's early `return true` at list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:190 fires whenever `silent && state.parentType === 'paragraph'`, with the only positional constraint being `state.sCount[line] >= state.blkIndent` (:32) — which is trivially satisfied at top level where `blkIndent === 0`. So the change is not confined to the `#517` nested-dash shape: paragraph text such as `see below *` or `note +`, which upstream markdown-it renders as lazy continuation inside the `

`, now terminates the paragraph and emits a stray empty `

`. Nothing in the diff's `- 1 -` framing, the design note, or the five added tests exercises a `*`/`+` marker or a top-level (unindented) empty bullet, so this consumer-visible behaviour change to arbitrary existing note bodies was not considered. Fix belongs on the new code: either restrict `isEmptyBulletLine` to the dash marker that `lheading` actually contends for, or require an enclosing list context.

findings.summary: `getRuleFn` reads markdown-it's private `__rules__` registry and throws at module-import time, so a markdown-it upgrade takes down the whole notes preview rather than degrading one rendering case
findings.evidence: `const rule = ruler.__rules__.find((r) => r.name === name);` / `if (!rule) throw new Error(...)` at list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:211-212, reached from `listEmptyBulletPlugin` (:179) which `preview.ts` invokes via `md.use(listEmptyBulletPlugin)` at module scope (preview.ts:47, alongside the module-level `const md = new MarkdownIt(...)` at preview.ts:12). Because the `md.use(...)` calls run during module evaluation, this `throw` is not a rendering fallback — it is an import-time crash of `preview.ts` and therefore of every consumer that imports `NotePreview`. `__rules__` is not part of markdown-it's public API (the file's own comment at :203 concedes `markdown-it's Ruler exposes no public getter`), and the copied `lheadingRule` is likewise pinned to 14.x internals (`state.skipChars`, `state.getLines`, `getRules('paragraph')`). Any dependency bump that renames the private field converts a cosmetic markdown deviation into a blank notes pane for all consumers. Fix belongs on the new code: recover the stock rule without private access (e.g. import `markdown-it/lib/rules_block/list`, or degrade gracefully instead of throwing).

findings.summary: Other render paths for the same note content (export/print/excerpt/server-side, or the 'shared markdown model' the docs reference) are not given this plugin, so one document will render two ways
findings.evidence: The plugin is wired only into the single `md` instance in `packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts` (`md.use(listEmptyBulletPlugin);` at preview.ts:47). The design note added by this change explicitly frames the deviation as `a notes-preview-only rendering choice, not a change to the shared markdown model` (docs/design/notes/notes.md), which concedes that a second markdown consumer exists. Any other consumer of note markdown — an HTML/PDF export, a note-card excerpt renderer, a search-snippet stripper, or the Wafflebase-side renderer discussed in the same doc's `P3 — CodePair → Wafflebase migration` section — still runs stock `lheading` and will keep emitting `<h2>` for `- 1\n  -`, so the preview and the exported/shared rendering of the identical stored document now disagree. I could not confirm which of those paths exist: only `scripts/` is materialised in this checkout, so every cross-reference grep for `packages/notes`, `NotePreview`, `MarkdownIt`, `block.ruler` and `listEmptyBulletPlugin` returned zero files. To confirm, grep the full tree for `new MarkdownIt(`, `markdown-it` imports outside `packages/notes/src/view/`, and any importer of `preview.ts`.

findings.summary: `Ruler.at('lheading', ...)` is called without an `options.alt`, discarding whatever alt chain the installed markdown-it registers for `lheading`
findings.evidence: `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', lheadingRule);` at list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:175 passes no options, while the very next `at()` call (:197-199) does pass `{ alt: ['paragraph','reference','blockquote'] }` precisely because, as the change's own lessons file records, `Ruler.at(name, fn, options)` REPLACES the rule's \`alt\` chain with \`options.alt || []\` (docs/tasks/active/20260724-notes-empty-bullet-setext-lessons.md:19). The author applied that lesson to `list` and not to `lheading`. In markdown-it 14.x's `parser_block` registry `lheading` is declared with no alt chain, so this is likely harmless today — but it is an unguarded assumption about a third-party private table, and if the pinned version (or a future bump) gives `lheading` any alt membership, it silently stops terminating paragraphs/blockquotes/references for consumers well outside this file. To confirm, check `node_modules/markdown-it/lib/parser_block.mjs` for the `lheading` entry's third element. Fix belongs on the new code: pass the upstream alt chain back explicitly, as was done for `list`.

findings.summary: Plugin ordering: `listEmptyBulletPlugin` runs after `detailsPlugin` and re-registers `list`/`lheading`, clobbering any alt chain or wrapper those earlier plugins installed on the same rules
findings.evidence: `preview.ts` applies plugins in sequence — `md.use(detailsPlugin)` (preview.ts:43) then `md.use(listEmptyBulletPlugin)` (preview.ts:47) — and the new plugin calls `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', ...)` (list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:175) and `md.block.ruler.at('list', ...)` (:197) which overwrite both the fn and the alt chain of those rules. `getRuleFn(md, 'list')` (:179) captures whatever fn is installed at that moment, so a `list` wrapper from `detailsPlugin` survives, but `lheading` is replaced outright with no delegation and the restored `alt` for `list` is hardcoded to markdown-it's stock `['paragraph','reference','blockquote']` — dropping any alt membership (e.g. a `details` context) an earlier plugin added. `details-plugin.ts` is not in the diff and is not present in this checkout, so I could not verify whether it touches `list`/`lheading`; the new file's header comment references it (`same note as in \`details-plugin.ts\``), confirming it exists. To confirm, open `packages/notes/src/view/details-plugin.ts` and grep it for `block.ruler`, `ruler.at`, `ruler.before`, and `alt:`.

findings.summary: A throw from `getRuleFn` at module scope takes down the entire `@wafflebase/notes` public entry point, not just the preview — including the store and toolbar surfaces that never touch markdown.
findings.evidence: `getRuleFn` (packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:212) throws `markdown-it block rule not found: list` if markdown-it's private `__rules__` registry shape changes. It is invoked from `md.use(listEmptyBulletPlugin)` at preview.ts:48, which is *module top-level*. The out-of-diff blast radius is the import chain: packages/notes/src/index.ts:12 re-exports `initialize` from `./view/editor.js`, and packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:20 statically imports `NotePreview` from `./preview.js`. So evaluating the package barrel evaluates preview.ts. Every frontend consumer therefore fails to import, not just the preview pane: packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:7, notes-detail.tsx:9, notes-toolbar.tsx:7, and yorkie-note-store.ts:7 (the Yorkie CRDT note store, which has nothing to do with markdown rendering). `packages/notes/package.json:63` pins `"markdown-it": "^14.1.0"` (caret) and harness.config.json:45 enables `dependencyFreshness` with `failOnCritical`, so an automated bump is a live path. Fix belongs on the new code: make `getRuleFn` degrade (return a no-op / skip the wrap) instead of throwing during module evaluation, or move the `md.use` behind a lazily-initialised renderer.

findings.summary: The lone-dash setext exemption is unconditional (not scoped to list context), so every existing note using the valid single-dash setext H2 form `Title\n-` silently stops rendering as a heading.
findings.evidence:
`const isLoneDash = marker === DASH && runLength === 1;` at list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:104 has no guard on `state.blkIndent`, `state.parentType`, or whether a list is open. It fires identically for a top-level `Title\n-`, which is a perfectly ordinary CommonMark setext H2. Note content is stored as raw markdown in Yorkie (docs/design/notes/notes.md:96 — "one flat string in one `Text` CRDT"), so this re-renders *all already-stored* notes, not just newly typed ones: the heading becomes a paragraph followed by a stray empty `
`. The consumer left describing the old contract is docs/design/notes/notes.md:296-297, which asserts "Multi-dash `---` and `=` setext underlines are untouched, so ordinary setext headings still render" — single-dash setext headings are ordinary setext headings and no longer render. The change's own plan file (docs/tasks/active/20260724-notes-empty-bullet-setext-todo.md:62) lists "top-level lone dash" as a case to cover, and no test in the added block (preview.test.ts:151-196) exercises it. Consider gating `isLoneDash` on being inside a list / non-zero `blkIndent`.

findings.summary: The CodeMirror source pane still parses these lines as setext headings, so in split view the editor and the preview now disagree about the same text.
findings.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:200 installs `markdown()` from `@codemirror/lang-markdown` (imported at editor.ts:8), whose Lezer grammar is strict CommonMark and was not touched by this change. `initialize` mounts both panes side by side (editor.ts:117 `new NotePreview()`, editor.ts:144 `container.appendChild(preview.el)`), and `both` is a documented layout mode (editor.ts:36). After this change, typing `- 1\n  -` (or `Title\n-`) leaves the left pane styling the line above as a heading via the markdown language's `SetextHeading` node while the right pane renders body text plus an empty bullet. This is an out-of-diff consumer of the same markdown contract that was not updated alongside the preview deviation.

findings.summary: The paragraph-interrupt relaxation also covers `*` and `+` markers, a wider CommonMark deviation than the `-`-only scope the design doc and plugin docblock promise.
findings.evidence:
`isEmptyBulletLine` (list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:38-40) accepts `-`, `0x2a /* * */` and `0x2b /* + */`, and `wrappedList` returns `true` for all three. `*` and `+` are never setext underlines, so issue #517 does not require relaxing them — yet `foo\n*` and `foo\n+`, which previously rendered as lazy-continuation text `foo
*`, now terminate the paragraph and emit an empty list. The scope statement this contradicts is docs/design/notes/notes.md:293-296 ("a **lone single `-`** ... is never a setext underline") and the plugin docblock at list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:158-172. No added test covers `*`/`+` (preview.test.ts:151-196 uses only `-`), so the widened deviation is invisible.

findings.summary: `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', ...)` omits the `alt`-restoration the same file's own lessons note flags as mandatory, an asymmetry with the `list` call two lines below.
findings.evidence: list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:175 calls `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', lheadingRule)` with no options, while lines 196-198 deliberately pass `{ alt: ['paragraph','reference','blockquote'] }` when replacing `list`, with a comment explaining that `Ruler.at` resets the alt chain. docs/tasks/active/20260724-notes-empty-bullet-setext-lessons.md:18-21 records this exact hazard. It is currently harmless because markdown-it 14's `lheading` is registered with no alt chain, but the invariant is now maintained by hand in one of two places and is silently coupled to an upstream registration detail — a markdown-it version that gives `lheading` an alt chain would have it wiped with no signal. Add the explicit `{ alt: [] }` plus a comment, or a note explaining why lheading needs none.

findings.summary: `isEmptyBulletLine` has no 4-space indent ceiling, so a deeply indented lone dash after a paragraph now terminates it and can become an indented code block instead of lazy text.
findings.evidence:
`isEmptyBulletLine` (list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:22) only checks `state.sCount[line] < state.blkIndent` (a floor), never the `sCount - blkIndent >= 4` code-block ceiling that both the upstream `list` rule and the vendored `lheadingRule` (line 78, line 85) apply. For input like `foo\n -` (4-space indent, not inside a list) `wrappedList` returns `true` in silent mode, ending the paragraph; the `code` rule then claims the line, changing `foo
-` into a paragraph plus an indented code block containing `-`. This is outside the documented scope of the deviation (docs/design/notes/notes.md:293-299) and no added test covers it. Flagging as reachable-behaviour scope creep; the correctness lens may also own the condition itself.

findings.summary: Lone-dash relaxation is not scoped to list context, so top-level single-dash setext headings (`Title\n-`) stop rendering as <h2>
findings.evidence:
`const isLoneDash = marker === DASH && runLength === 1;` … `if (pos >= max && !isLoneDash)` unconditionally rejects a one-character `-` underline regardless of `state.blkIndent` / whether we are inside a list item. For input `Title\n-` at top level (blkIndent 0): upstream lheading sets level=2 → `

Title

`; with this rule the underline is skipped, the terminator chain then hits `wrappedList`, whose guard (`silent && parentType==='paragraph' && isEmptyBulletLine`) is satisfied because sCount[1]=0 >= blkIndent=0, so the paragraph terminates and the non-silent `list` rule builds an empty item — output becomes `

Title

`. A single `-` is a valid CommonMark setext H2 underline, and issue #517 is about an *indented, nested* empty bullet, so the relaxation could have been gated on being inside a list item / blkIndent > 0. The added tests only cover `Heading\n---` (multi-dash), and the task doc's own planned 'top-level lone dash' test is absent from preview.test.ts, so the regression is uncovered.

findings.summary: `isEmptyBulletLine` accepts `*` and `+`, widening the paragraph-interrupt deviation beyond the documented lone `-`
findings.evidence:
`if (marker !== DASH && marker !== 0x2a /* * */ && marker !== 0x2b /* + */) return false;` — the `lheading` relaxation only covers `-`, but the `list` interrupt relaxation covers all three bullet markers. Consequence: `foo *` and `foo +` (and `foo * `) previously stayed inside the paragraph as lazy text (`

foo *

`, since CommonMark forbids an empty bullet from interrupting a paragraph and `hr` needs 3 markers); they now terminate the paragraph and emit `
`. That contradicts docs/design/notes/notes.md, which describes the deviation as scoped to 'a lone single `-` (the empty-bullet shape)'. Nothing in the added tests covers `*`/`+`.

findings.summary: Hand-rolled `asciiTrim` diverges from upstream lheading's `.trim()` for non-ASCII whitespace
findings.evidence: `const content = asciiTrim(state.getLines(...))` with `ASCII_TRIM_RE = /^[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+|[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+$/g`. markdown-it's `rules_block/lheading` uses `String.prototype.trim()`, which also strips Unicode whitespace (U+00A0 NBSP, U+2028/29, U+FEFF, other Zs). So for `Heading \n===` this copy keeps the trailing NBSP in the heading's inline content where stock markdown-it would drop it — a silent behavioral divergence in a rule that is supposed to be a faithful mirror. The accompanying comment ('ASCII whitespace trimmed by markdown-it's own `asciiTrim`') also appears to describe a helper markdown-it does not have, which is what makes the divergence easy to miss.

findings.summary: `getRuleFn` throws from module-initialization scope, so an internals change turns a degraded feature into a hard import failure of the whole preview module
findings.evidence: `const rule = ruler.__rules__.find((r) => r.name === name); if (!rule) throw new Error(...)`. `listEmptyBulletPlugin` is invoked by `md.use(listEmptyBulletPlugin)` at top level of preview.ts (module side effect, no try/catch), and `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', ...)` likewise throws 'Parser rule not found' if the name is gone. If markdown-it renames/reshapes the private `__rules__` registry (or a plugin removes `list`), importing preview.ts throws and the entire notes preview fails to load rather than just losing the #517 nicety. A defensive fallback (skip the wrapping) would keep the failure local.

findings.summary: Hard-coded `alt: ['paragraph','reference','blockquote']` overwrites whatever alt chain `list` actually had at plugin-apply time
findings.evidence: `md.block.ruler.at('list', wrappedList, { alt: ['paragraph', 'reference', 'blockquote'] });` restores the alt chain from a literal instead of reading the existing entry's `alt` (which `getRuleFn` is already positioned to return alongside `fn`). `listEmptyBulletPlugin` is applied last in preview.ts, after taskLists, katexPlugin and detailsPlugin; any alt entry one of those (or a future plugin, or a future markdown-it version) added to `list` is silently dropped, and `list` would stop terminating that block type. Reading and reusing the current `alt` array removes the coupling.

findings.summary: Silent shortcut returns `true` without replicating the stock list rule's own indent guards, so it can claim a line where no list can actually start
findings.evidence: `if (silent && state.parentType === 'paragraph' && isEmptyBulletLine(state, startLine)) return true;` bypasses `originalList` entirely. `isEmptyBulletLine` only checks `sCount[line] >= blkIndent`; the real `list` rule additionally bails on `state.sCount[startLine] - state.blkIndent >= 4` (code block) and on the `state.listIndent >= 0 && sCount - listIndent >= 4 && sCount < blkIndent` lazy-continuation case. Today those combinations are unreachable because every caller of the 'paragraph' terminator chain (`paragraph`, this `lheading` copy, `reference`) `continue`s on `sCount - blkIndent > 3`, but the wrapper is now the contract for any future/plugin caller of that chain: a 4+-space-indented lone bullet would terminate the paragraph while the following non-silent pass refuses to build a list, leaving a stray `-` paragraph or indented code where lazy text was expected. Mirroring the two guards inside `isEmptyBulletLine` would make the shortcut agree with the rule it front-runs.

findings.summary: `at('lheading', lheadingRule)` is called without options, which clears that rule's alt chain
findings.evidence: `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', lheadingRule);` — the change's own lessons doc notes that `Ruler.at(name, fn, options)` replaces `alt` with `options.alt || []`, and it compensates for `list` but not for `lheading`. In markdown-it 14 `lheading` is registered with no alt list, so this is a no-op there; if the installed version (the docs claim 'markdown-it 14.3.0') registers `lheading` with any alt membership, replacing it here silently removes it and `lheading` stops terminating that block type. Passing the existing `alt` back, as done for `list`, would make this robust rather than version-dependent.

findings.summary: `isLoneDash` disables single-dash setext headings everywhere, not just inside list items — `Title\n-` loses its `<h2>` and emits a stray empty bullet
findings.evidence:
Line 105: `const isLoneDash = marker === DASH && runLength === 1;` and line 107 `if (pos >= max && !isLoneDash)`. The guard has no context condition (no check that the dash line is indented deeper than the paragraph, or that `state.parentType`/`state.listIndent` indicates we are inside a list item). Consequence for top-level input `Title\n-`: lheadingRule declines the underline, the terminator loop then calls the wrapped `list` (which returns true for the lone `-`), lheading returns false, `paragraph` consumes `Title` and stops at line 1, and the non-silent `list` rule builds an empty item. Output becomes `

Title

` instead of `

Title

` — the heading is silently downgraded AND the `-` character disappears from the rendered text. Issue #517 only concerns an *indented* empty bullet under a list item; nothing in the fix restricts the deviation to that shape. The tests only cover the multi-dash form (`Heading\n---`), so this regression is untested.

findings.summary: Paragraph-interrupt relaxation accepts `*`/`+` and applies to any paragraph, so a literal marker character in body text is silently dropped from the rendered output
findings.evidence:
`wrappedList` (lines 182-191) returns `true` for *any* line satisfying `isEmptyBulletLine`, and `isEmptyBulletLine` (line 39) accepts `-`, `*` and `+`, with the only positional constraint being `state.sCount[line] >= state.blkIndent` (line 32). CommonMark/markdown-it deliberately renders `foo\n*` as `

foo\n*

` (an empty bullet may not interrupt a paragraph). With this plugin the paragraph terminates and the non-silent `list` rule builds an empty item, so the output is `

foo

` — the `*` (or `+`, or `-`) glyph the user typed is no longer rendered anywhere. That is user-visible content loss in ordinary prose, well beyond the documented deviation (docs/design/notes/notes.md describes only 'a lone single `-`'), and there is no test for the `*`/`+` or top-level cases.

findings.summary: `isEmptyBulletLine` omits the guards the real `list` rule applies, so the silent 'yes' can disagree with what the non-silent `list` rule will do
findings.evidence: `isEmptyBulletLine` only checks `state.sCount[line] < state.blkIndent` (line 32). markdown-it's `list` rule additionally rejects `state.sCount[line] - state.blkIndent >= 4` (indented code block) and the `state.listIndent >= 0 && sCount - listIndent >= 4 && sCount < blkIndent` special case. So `wrappedList` can report 'this empty bullet terminates the paragraph' for a line that non-silent `list` will refuse, after which `code`/`paragraph` claims it instead — the paragraph is split for nothing. Today this is masked only because `paragraph`/`lheadingRule` `continue` on lines with `sCount - blkIndent > 3` before consulting terminators (line 86); the invariant is implicit and any future caller (another plugin registering `alt: ['paragraph']`, or a rule that sets `parentType = 'paragraph'`) reaches the unguarded path. Mirroring list's own two guards inside `isEmptyBulletLine` would make silent and non-silent agree by construction.

findings.summary: Re-registration hard-codes `list`'s `alt` chain and reads markdown-it's private `__rules__`; both fail silently/at import time if internals or another plugin differ
findings.evidence: Line 197-199 calls `md.block.ruler.at('list', wrappedList, { alt: ['paragraph', 'reference', 'blockquote'] })`, restoring a literal copy of upstream's alt list rather than the value actually in effect. Any plugin loaded earlier that added to `list`'s alt chain (or a markdown-it version whose chain differs) has its entry silently dropped, and `list` stops acting as a terminator for that chain — a quiet rendering bug with no error. Compounding it, `getRuleFn` (lines 207-213) reaches into the undocumented `ruler.__rules__` and `throw`s `markdown-it block rule not found` on mismatch; because `preview.ts` calls `md.use(listEmptyBulletPlugin)` at module scope, that throw happens at import time and takes down the entire notes preview module rather than degrading. Reading the existing alt chain from `__rules__` (already being accessed) and passing it back would remove the duplication risk.

findings.summary: `asciiTrim` is narrower than the `.trim()` upstream `lheading` uses, so setext heading content with non-ASCII whitespace is trimmed differently
findings.evidence: Lines 19-23 define `ASCII_TRIM_RE` over `[\x09-\x0d\x20]` and line 134 applies it to `state.getLines(...)`. markdown-it 14's `rules_block/lheading.mjs` uses JS `String.prototype.trim()`, which also strips U+00A0, U+2028/9, U+FEFF etc. A setext heading whose content begins/ends with a NBSP therefore keeps that character here but not upstream. Also, the comment claims this re-creates "markdown-it's own `asciiTrim`"; I could not find such an export in markdown-it's public or common utils, so the stated justification for diverging from `.trim()` looks unverified.

samples.summary: Silent shortcut returns `true` without replicating the stock list rule's own indent guards, so it can claim a line where no list can actually start
samples.evidence: `if (silent && state.parentType === 'paragraph' && isEmptyBulletLine(state, startLine)) return true;` bypasses `originalList` entirely. `isEmptyBulletLine` only checks `sCount[line] >= blkIndent`; the real `list` rule additionally bails on `state.sCount[startLine] - state.blkIndent >= 4` (code block) and on the `state.listIndent >= 0 && sCount - listIndent >= 4 && sCount < blkIndent` lazy-continuation case. Today those combinations are unreachable because every caller of the 'paragraph' terminator chain (`paragraph`, this `lheading` copy, `reference`) `continue`s on `sCount - blkIndent > 3`, but the wrapper is now the contract for any future/plugin caller of that chain: a 4+-space-indented lone bullet would terminate the paragraph while the following non-silent pass refuses to build a list, leaving a stray `-` paragraph or indented code where lazy text was expected. Mirroring the two guards inside `isEmptyBulletLine` would make the shortcut agree with the rule it front-runs.

samples.summary: `at('lheading', lheadingRule)` is called without options, which clears that rule's alt chain
samples.evidence: `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', lheadingRule);` — the change's own lessons doc notes that `Ruler.at(name, fn, options)` replaces `alt` with `options.alt || []`, and it compensates for `list` but not for `lheading`. In markdown-it 14 `lheading` is registered with no alt list, so this is a no-op there; if the installed version (the docs claim 'markdown-it 14.3.0') registers `lheading` with any alt membership, replacing it here silently removes it and `lheading` stops terminating that block type. Passing the existing `alt` back, as done for `list`, would make this robust rather than version-dependent.

samples.summary: Paragraph-interrupt relaxation accepts `*`/`+` and applies to any paragraph, so a literal marker character in body text is silently dropped from the rendered output
samples.evidence:
`wrappedList` (lines 182-191) returns `true` for *any* line satisfying `isEmptyBulletLine`, and `isEmptyBulletLine` (line 39) accepts `-`, `*` and `+`, with the only positional constraint being `state.sCount[line] >= state.blkIndent` (line 32). CommonMark/markdown-it deliberately renders `foo\n*` as `

` (an empty bullet may not interrupt a paragraph). With this plugin the paragraph terminates and the non-silent `list` rule builds an empty item, so the output is `

samples.summary: `isEmptyBulletLine` omits the guards the real `list` rule applies, so the silent 'yes' can disagree with what the non-silent `list` rule will do
samples.evidence: `isEmptyBulletLine` only checks `state.sCount[line] < state.blkIndent` (line 32). markdown-it's `list` rule additionally rejects `state.sCount[line] - state.blkIndent >= 4` (indented code block) and the `state.listIndent >= 0 && sCount - listIndent >= 4 && sCount < blkIndent` special case. So `wrappedList` can report 'this empty bullet terminates the paragraph' for a line that non-silent `list` will refuse, after which `code`/`paragraph` claims it instead — the paragraph is split for nothing. Today this is masked only because `paragraph`/`lheadingRule` `continue` on lines with `sCount - blkIndent > 3` before consulting terminators (line 86); the invariant is implicit and any future caller (another plugin registering `alt: ['paragraph']`, or a rule that sets `parentType = 'paragraph'`) reaches the unguarded path. Mirroring list's own two guards inside `isEmptyBulletLine` would make silent and non-silent agree by construction.

samples.summary: Re-registration hard-codes `list`'s `alt` chain and reads markdown-it's private `__rules__`; both fail silently/at import time if internals or another plugin differ
samples.evidence: Line 197-199 calls `md.block.ruler.at('list', wrappedList, { alt: ['paragraph', 'reference', 'blockquote'] })`, restoring a literal copy of upstream's alt list rather than the value actually in effect. Any plugin loaded earlier that added to `list`'s alt chain (or a markdown-it version whose chain differs) has its entry silently dropped, and `list` stops acting as a terminator for that chain — a quiet rendering bug with no error. Compounding it, `getRuleFn` (lines 207-213) reaches into the undocumented `ruler.__rules__` and `throw`s `markdown-it block rule not found` on mismatch; because `preview.ts` calls `md.use(listEmptyBulletPlugin)` at module scope, that throw happens at import time and takes down the entire notes preview module rather than degrading. Reading the existing alt chain from `__rules__` (already being accessed) and passing it back would remove the duplication risk.

samples.summary: `asciiTrim` is narrower than the `.trim()` upstream `lheading` uses, so setext heading content with non-ASCII whitespace is trimmed differently
samples.evidence: Lines 19-23 define `ASCII_TRIM_RE` over `[\x09-\x0d\x20]` and line 134 applies it to `state.getLines(...)`. markdown-it 14's `rules_block/lheading.mjs` uses JS `String.prototype.trim()`, which also strips U+00A0, U+2028/9, U+FEFF etc. A setext heading whose content begins/ends with a NBSP therefore keeps that character here but not upstream. Also, the comment claims this re-creates "markdown-it's own `asciiTrim`"; I could not find such an export in markdown-it's public or common utils, so the stated justification for diverging from `.trim()` looks unverified.
